transcript.text: Hi there! I'd love to figure out your personality type through a quick chat. To start, tell me about the last time you were around a lot of people for a long time. How did you feel afterwards?

Oh, that was probably my niece's birthday party last weekend with about thirty relatives running around. By the time I finally got home, I just wanted to change into my comfortable sweatpants and sit quietly with a hot cup of tea. It was lovely seeing everyone, but it definitely took a lot out of me!
It sounds like that tea and quiet time were much needed after a bustling party! When your mind wanders and nothing is demanding your attention, what do you usually find yourself thinking about?

I'm usually running through my mental checklist for the upcoming week, like what groceries we need for Thursday's potluck or when I need to schedule the car's oil change. Sometimes I'll also just find myself reminiscing about past family traditions and making sure I have all the right ingredients saved for our traditional holiday pie.

Planning ahead and keeping track of all those practical details keeps things running smoothly. Tell me about a time you had to give someone news or feedback they wouldn't like. What went through your mind and what did you actually do?

Oh, I really hate having to upset anyone, so I lose sleep over things like that. Last month I had to tell a neighbor that their tree roots were lifting our shared fence, and I practiced what I was going to say in the mirror three times. When I finally went over, I brought along a batch of fresh oatmeal raisin cookies to soften the blow and made sure to keep my voice very kind and calm.
Planning a trip takes quite a bit of coordination. How do you usually go about organizing your itinerary, and what happens to your day if something unexpected suddenly throws off your schedule?

I always map out our daily schedule on a printed spreadsheet weeks in advance, including meal reservations and travel times. If something unexpected throws it off, like a sudden rainstorm or a flat tire, I get a knot in my stomach and quickly consult my backup plan to get us back on track.
It is so helpful to have backup plans ready when surprises happen. Tell me about something that caught your curiosity lately and made you want to dive in and learn more about how it works.

I got really curious about canning and preserving our garden tomatoes last month, so I borrowed a trusted step-by-step guide from the local library. I spent the whole Saturday sterilizing jars and following the boiling-water bath instructions to the letter so everything would be safe and last through the winter.
